transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help with any questions you may have about your cataract surgery recovery. How are you feeling after your surgery? Do you have any questions about your recovery or anything else?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Thanks for asking. I'm feeling okay, but I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
According to the information I have, you should avoid any exercise for 1 week after surgery, but you can then go back to light exercise, such as brisk walking, gardening, light jogging, and gentle cycling. So, after 1 week, you should be able to start doing a little bit of gardening, but remember to be gentle and avoid any heavy lifting or bending.

Do you have any other questions about your recovery or gardening?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That makes sense. Thank you! My next question is when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
You should continue to use the eye drops as was prescribed. If you're running out, your GP should be able to provide some more. And if you were using any eye drops before your operation, such as for glaucoma, or for dry eyes, it's safe to continue using them, unless you've been told otherwise.

So, you can keep using your eye drops as usual. If you have any questions about the specific drops you're using or how to use them, you might want to check the instructions on the bottle or ask your GP for clarification.

Do you have any other questions about your eye drops or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for that information. I was wondering—I'm very sensitive to bright light right now; is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
It's normal for the eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to the new lenses. Mild sensitivity to bright light is common, and wearing sunglasses when you're going outside can help. However, if you're experiencing significant pain when it's bright or severe light sensitivity, especially if your eye is also red and painful, we may need to assess this further. Does that make sense?

Do you have any other questions about your light sensitivity or recovery?
